turns.prompt: Build an original simple 3D costume shell in Blender using the garment-section schematic and the kimono's quiet body/red boundary as references. The schematic is an authored clearance diagram, not a physically simulated garment. Show A with a folded shoulder-to-waist shell and B with a softer layered shell, on the same simple mannequin and under the same camera and lighting. The outer shell should visibly anchor at the shoulders, leave clearance around the torso and forearms, and have a readable lower edge rather than intersecting the body. Preserve the mannequin's proportions in both directions. Expose shell offset, fold depth, and lower-edge flare in source.py; demonstrate a real shell-offset parameter edit while keeping the camera and mannequin fixed. Include a side render and distinguish modeled clearance from untested cloth simulation or VRM rigging. Deliver scene.blend, source.py, a.png, b.png, side.png, parameter-probe.png, evidence.json, notes.md. Keep these filenames on every turn. PNG previews must use the declared dimensions; include actual rendered results, not an empty placeholder. All four PNGs are actual 640x480 Blender renders. Save both labeled alternatives in scene.blend; expose meaningful parameters in source.py and document a real parameter change and independent saved-scene reopen in evidence.json. Native scene editability is required; a flat drawing is insufficient.

Choose A for its shoulder attachment, not its lower width. Keep B unchanged. Refine only fold depth so the layered edge reads lighter without making the material transparent or widening the overall silhouette. Keep the shoulder anchors, mannequin, shell clearance, red-boundary palette, camera, and lighting. Deliver scene.blend, source.py, a.png, b.png, side.png, parameter-probe.png, evidence.json, notes.md. Keep these filenames on every turn. PNG previews must use the declared dimensions; include actual rendered results, not an empty placeholder. All four PNGs are actual 640x480 Blender renders. Save both labeled alternatives in scene.blend; expose meaningful parameters in source.py and document a real parameter change and independent saved-scene reopen in evidence.json. Native scene editability is required; a flat drawing is insufficient.

The front is good, but in side view the lower shell still cuts into the forearm space. Change only the lower-edge flare and local clearance there. Keep the accepted front shoulder outline, fold depth, torso proportions, palette, and camera. Repeat the same shell-offset parameter probe and reopen the native scene before rendering; do not describe it as a finished rig or a successful cloth simulation. Deliver scene.blend, source.py, a.png, b.png, side.png, parameter-probe.png, evidence.json, notes.md. Keep these filenames on every turn. PNG previews must use the declared dimensions; include actual rendered results, not an empty placeholder. All four PNGs are actual 640x480 Blender renders. Save both labeled alternatives in scene.blend; expose meaningful parameters in source.py and document a real parameter change and independent saved-scene reopen in evidence.json. Native scene editability is required; a flat drawing is insufficient.
